title: AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate (DEA-C01): The Cert That Proves You Can Build Data Platforms on AWS
tldr: AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate (DEA-C01) is AWS’s dedicated data engineering credential, launched in April 2024. Four domains, 65 questions, 130 minutes, 720/1000 to pass, $300 USD. Domain 1 — Data Ingestion and Transformation (34%) — carries the most weight: Glue ETL jobs and DynamicFrames, Kinesis Data Streams vs Firehose vs Flink Analytics, MSK Kafka pipelines, and converting JSON to Parquet for query efficiency. Domain 2 — Data Store Management (26%) — tests Redshift KEY/EVEN/ALL/AUTO distribution styles, sort key selection, Redshift Spectrum for S3 queries, DynamoDB single-table access patterns, and Aurora zero-ETL replication to Redshift. Domain 3 — Data Operations and Support (22%) — covers Glue Workflows, Amazon MWAA/Airflow, Step Functions orchestration, Glue job bookmarks for incremental loads, and CloudWatch pipeline monitoring. Domain 4 — Data Security and Governance (18%) — tests Lake Formation column-level, row-level, and cell-level controls, LF-Tags for attribute-based access control, AWS Macie PII detection, and SSE-KMS encryption strategy. DEA-C01 holders in 2026 earn $135k–$175k USD; senior practitioners report $180k–$220k total compensation in major US markets.
bodyHtml:
Data engineering got its own AWS cert

DEA-C01 launched in April 2024, replacing the Data Analytics Specialty as the primary AWS data engineering credential. The Associate tier targets production-relevant skills: Glue ETL, Kinesis streaming, Redshift warehousing, and Lake Formation governance — the four pillars of the AWS data platform stack used in enterprise data lakes today.

Domain 1 — Data Ingestion and Transformation (34%)

AWS Glue: three job types (Python Shell, ETL/Spark with DynamicFrames, Ray), Crawlers to populate the Data Catalog, job bookmarks for incremental processing, Glue Data Quality for completeness and uniqueness rules. Amazon Kinesis: Kinesis Data Streams (shard-based, custom consumers, millisecond latency, 24h–365d retention) vs Kinesis Firehose (managed delivery to S3/Redshift, buffer-and-batch, no consumer code, minimum operational overhead) vs Kinesis Analytics/Flink (stateful stream processing, windowing, anomaly detection). Amazon MSK for Kafka-API workloads with Schema Registry and Kafka Connect. Data formats: convert JSON to Parquet after landing — columnar compression reduces Athena scan costs 60–85%. Partition S3 data by date; compact small files to avoid listing overhead.

Domain 2 — Data Store Management (26%)

Amazon Redshift: KEY distribution collocates join rows on the same slice (use same key on both tables); EVEN distributes round-robin for staging tables; ALL copies small dimension tables to every node (star-schema optimization); AUTO lets Redshift choose. Compound sort keys accelerate range queries on leading columns. Redshift Spectrum queries cold S3 data via Glue Data Catalog without loading it into the warehouse. Aurora zero-ETL with Redshift replicates transactional data automatically, eliminating the Glue ETL job for OLTP→warehouse pipelines. DynamoDB for key-based millisecond access with DynamoDB Streams for change capture. Athena for serverless ad-hoc SQL over S3. OpenSearch for full-text and log analytics.

Domains 3 and 4 — Operations and Security

Domain 3: Glue Workflows for Glue-native pipelines; Amazon MWAA for complex Python DAG orchestration with custom operators; Step Functions for serverless state machines with visual debugging; EventBridge Scheduler for cron triggers. Cost optimization: EMR Spot Instances (60–90% savings), Redshift reserved nodes (75% savings), Athena partition pruning + Parquet. Domain 4: Lake Formation adds column-level, row-level, and cell-level security on top of S3 and the Glue Data Catalog — the correct answer over S3 bucket policies for multi-team data lake access at scale. LF-Tags for attribute-based access control across large catalogs. AWS Macie detects PII in S3 (detect only — remediate via EventBridge+Lambda). SSE-KMS for regulated data with CloudTrail audit of every decryption. VPC Gateway Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB; Interface Endpoints for Glue and Kinesis in production pipelines handling sensitive data.
